## Updates in Version 2.2026

::: {.white style="font-size: 0.6em; margin-top: 40px;"}
All recommendations are Category 2A unless otherwise indicated
:::


<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>PI3K Pathway Alterations & Aspirin:</strong><br>
For stage II and III, if somatic PI3K pathway alterations, start aspirin (unless contraindicated) 100–162 mg PO daily for 3 years after recovery from surgery (concurrent with chemotherapy if given).<br><br>
<strong>Molecular profiling should be done on all stage II and III CRC tumors.</strong>
</div>

**Somatic PI3K pathway alterations include:**
- Mutations in PIK3CA exon 9 and 20
- Other PIK3CA, PIK3R1, and PTEN mutations
- Deep deletions of PTEN

::: {.notes}
Also applies to REC-5, REC-6, REC-14
:::

## Updates in Version 1.2026


### Workup & Biomarkers
- **REC-2:** PIK3CA testing for somatic PI3K pathway alterations for stage II-III
- **REC-2A:** Biomarker testing as part of multigene panel testing (MGPT)
- **REC-2A:** Expanded to include POLE/POLD1, RET, NTRK 1/2/3

### Treatment Modifications
- **REC-3:** T1(favorable risk),N0 — branches for nonsurgical vs surgical candidate removed
- **REC-5:** pT3,N0,M0 adjuvant treatment modified — Consider FOLFOX or CAPEOX alone or Observation
- **REC-6:** Total neoadjuvant therapy options expanded

### New Immunotherapy Options
- **REC-F:** Additional checkpoint inhibitors added (penpulimab, atezolizumab, avelumab, cosibelimab, durvalumab)


## Initial Evaluation Framework

| Presentation | Workup | Next Step |
|-------------|--------|-----------|
| Polyp with invasive cancer | Pathology, colonoscopy, MMR/MSI | REC-1 |
| Without distant metastases | Biopsy, MRI, CT, CEA, biomarkers | REC-3 |
| With suspected/proven metastases | + Biomarker panel, consider PET/CT | REC-7 or REC-15 |

**Universal Testing:**
- MMR/MSI status
- PIK3CA for stage II-III (somatic PI3K pathway alterations)
- RAS/BRAF for metastatic disease

# REC-1: Polyp with Invasive Cancer

## Workup
- Pathology review (confirm pT1)
- Colonoscopy with marking of cancerous polyp site
- MMR/MSI testing

## Treatment Based on Findings

| Finding | Primary Treatment |
|---------|-----------------|
| Single specimen, completely removed, favorable histology, clear margins (pT1 only) | Observe OR Transanal local excision OR Transabdominal resection |
| Fragmented specimen, margin cannot be assessed, or unfavorable histologic features | Additional workup (EUS/MRI) → Transanal local excision OR Transabdominal resection |

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>Favorable features:</strong> No angiolymphatic invasion, submucosal invasion <1mm, low tumor budding, negative margin (>1mm)<br>
<strong>Unfavorable features:</strong> Angiolymphatic invasion, submucosal invasion >1mm, high tumor budding, positive margin
</div>

# REC-2: Workup Without Distant Metastases

## Required Evaluations

::: {.incremental}
- **Biopsy** — confirm adenocarcinoma
- **MMR/MSI testing**
- **PIK3CA testing** for stage II-III (somatic PI3K pathway alterations)
- **Pathology review**
- **Colonoscopy** — complete to cecum
- **Consider proctoscopy**
- **Chest CT + Abdominal CT or MRI**
- **CBC, chemistry profile, CEA**
- **Pelvis MRI with or without contrast** (preferred for local staging)
- **Endorectal ultrasound** (if MRI contraindicated/inconclusive, or for T1 lesions)
- **Enterostomal therapist** — preoperative marking
- **FDG-PET/CT is NOT indicated**
- **Multidisciplinary team evaluation**
- **Fertility risk discussion**
:::

# REC-2A: Workup With Suspected/Proven Distant Metastases

## Additional Requirements

### Biomarker Testing (order rapidly)
- **RAS** (KRAS, NRAS) and **BRAF V600E** mutations
- **HER2 (ERBB2)** overexpression/amplification
- **MMR or MSI** status (if not previously done)
- **Multigene panel testing (MGPT)** — identifies rare actionable mutations:
  - POLE/POLD1
  - RET
  - NTRK 1/2/3

### Additional Workup
- Consider FDG-PET/CT if potentially surgically curable M1
- Consider MRI of liver for potentially resectable disease
- Multidisciplinary evaluation including experienced surgeon

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Pathway split:</strong> pMMR/MSS → REC-7 | dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1 mutation → REC-15
</div>

# REC-3: Staging & Primary Treatment

## Without Suspected/Proven Distant Metastases

| Clinical Stage | Primary Treatment |
|---------------|-------------------|
| **T1 (favorable risk), N0** | ESD or Transanal local excision OR Transabdominal resection |
| **T1 (high risk), T2, N0** | Transabdominal resection (preferred) OR Long-course chemo/RT → Consider FOLFOX/CAPEOX → Restaging → Resection |
| **T3, N any; T1-2, N1-2; T4, N any** | See REC-3A |

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>High-risk T1 features:</strong> Positive margins, lymphovascular invasion, poorly differentiated, sm3 invasion<br>
<strong>Short-course RT:</strong> Consider for preoperative radiation; however, for high-risk rectal cancer (cT4a/b, EMVI, cN2, involved MRF), 5-year RAPIDO follow-up shows statistically higher locoregional recurrence (10% vs 6%)
</div>

# REC-3A: Advanced Staging Decisions

## For T3, N Any; T1-2, N1-2; T4, N Any or Locally Unresectable

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>For stage II and III, if somatic PI3K pathway alterations:</strong><br>
Start aspirin 100–162 mg PO daily for 3 years after recovery from surgery (concurrent with chemotherapy if given)
</div>

### Pathway Split:

| Biomarker Status | Destination |
|-----------------|-------------|
| **pMMR/MSS** | REC-6 (Primary Treatment) |
| **dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1 mutation with ultra-hypermutated phenotype (TMB >50 mut/Mb)** | REC-14 (Primary Treatment) |

### T3, N0 Low-Risk, High Rectal Tumors
- Transabdominal resection OR
- Treat as T3, N any below

# REC-4: After Transanal Local Excision (T1,N0)

## Pathologic Findings & Adjuvant Treatment

| Finding | Management |
|---------|-----------|
| **pT1, NX without high-risk features** | Observe → Surveillance |
| **pT1, NX with high-risk features OR pT2, NX** | Transabdominal resection (preferred) OR Long-course chemo/RT → Consider FOLFOX/CAPEOX → Restaging → Resection |

<div class="important-box">
<strong>High-risk features:</strong> Positive margins, lymphovascular invasion, poorly differentiated tumors, sm3 invasion
</div>

**Complete clinical response option:**
- If complete clinical response after neoadjuvant therapy, consider surveillance (watch and wait) in experienced centers

# REC-5: After Transabdominal Resection (T1-2,N0)

## Adjuvant Treatment (Up to 6 Months Perioperative)

| Pathology | Treatment |
|-----------|-----------|
| **pT1-2, N0, M0** | Observe |
| **pT3, N0, M0** | Long-course chemo/RT → Chemotherapy (FOLFOX/CAPEOX) OR Chemotherapy alone (FOLFOX/CAPEOX) OR FOLFOX/CAPEOX alone OR Observation* |
| **pT4, N0, M0 or pT1-4, N1-2** | Long-course chemo/RT → Chemotherapy OR Chemotherapy → Long-course chemo/RT OR Consider FOLFOX/CAPEOX alone (pT1-3, N1 only) |

<div class="warning-box">
*Observation can be considered in select pT3N0 patients: well-differentiated or moderately well-differentiated, <2mm mesorectal invasion, no lymphatic/venous involvement, upper rectum
</div>

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Postoperative RT should be highly selective</strong> (e.g., for incomplete mesorectal grade) due to severe toxicity concerns
</div>

# pMMR/MSS Rectal Cancer: Overview

## Treatment Algorithm Structure

::: {.incremental}
1. **Localized Disease** (REC-6)
   - T3, N any; T1-2, N1-2; T4, N any
   - Total neoadjuvant therapy approach

2. **Synchronous Metastatic** (REC-7)
   - Liver only and/or lung only
   - Abdominal/peritoneal metastases
   - Unresectable other sites

3. **Recurrence/Metachronous** (REC-11 through REC-13)
   - Isolated pelvic/anastomotic recurrence
   - Resectable metachronous metastases
   - Unresectable metachronous metastases
:::

# REC-6: pMMR/MSS — Locally Advanced

## Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT)

### Option 1: Chemo/RT → Chemotherapy
- Long-course chemo/RT (capecitabine or infusional 5-FU) OR Short-course RT
- → Chemotherapy (12-16 weeks): FOLFOX or CAPEOX (preferred), Consider FOLFIRINOX
- → Restaging → Resection or Surveillance (if cCR)

### Option 2: Chemotherapy → Chemo/RT
- Chemotherapy (12-16 weeks): FOLFOX or CAPEOX (preferred), Consider FOLFIRINOX
- → Long-course chemo/RT OR Short-course RT
- → Restaging → Resection

### Option 3: Chemotherapy for Non-T4 (Sphincter-Sparing)
- Chemotherapy (12-16 weeks): FOLFOX or CAPEOX
- → Restage with sigmoidoscopy ± MRI
- → If tumor regression >20%: Surgery
- → If tumor regression ≤20% or high-risk features remain: Consider additional chemo/RT

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Complete clinical response:</strong> Consider surveillance (REC-10A) — watch and wait in experienced multidisciplinary centers
</div>

# REC-7: pMMR/MSS — Synchronous Metastatic

## Initial Stratification

| Finding | Primary Treatment |
|---------|-------------------|
| **Resectable liver only and/or lung only** | REC-8 |
| **Unresectable or medically inoperable liver/lung** | REC-9 |
| **Synchronous abdominal/peritoneal metastases** | Systemic therapy or Palliative management |
| **Synchronous unresectable other sites** | Systemic therapy (REC-F) |

### Nonobstructing Primary Tumor
→ Systemic therapy (REC-F)

### Obstructed or Imminent Obstruction
→ Resection OR Diverting ostomy OR Bowel bypass OR Stenting (upper rectal lesions only) → Systemic therapy

# REC-8: Resectable Synchronous Liver/Lung Metastases (pMMR/MSS)

## Neoadjuvant Treatment Approach

### Upfront Chemotherapy (Preferred)
- **FOLFOX** (preferred) or **CAPEOX** (preferred)
- OR Fluorouracil/leucovorin or Capecitabine
- OR **FOLFIRINOX**

→ Restaging → 

| Response | Next Step |
|----------|-----------|
| Good response | Consider holding radiation → Staged/synchronous resection and/or local therapy |
| Need for pelvic control | Short-course RT OR Long-course chemo/RT + pelvis RT |

### Upfront Radiation
- Short-course RT OR Long-course chemo/RT + pelvis RT
- → Chemotherapy (FOLFOX/CAPEOX preferred)
- → Restaging (best tumor response 8 weeks after RT completion)

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Local therapy options:</strong> Resection preferred for liver; thermal ablation equivalent for lesions ≤3cm; SBRT for lung metastases
</div>

# REC-9: Unresectable Synchronous Liver/Lung (pMMR/MSS)

## Systemic Therapy Options

### First-Line
- **(FOLFIRI or irinotecan) ± bevacizumab [preferred]** OR ziv-aflibercept OR ramucirumab
- **(FOLFIRI or irinotecan) ± cetuximab or panitumumab** (KRAS/NRAS/BRAF WT only)
- **Encorafenib + (cetuximab or panitumumab)** (BRAF V600E mutation)
- **(Pertuzumab or tucatinib) + trastuzumab** (HER2+ and KRAS/NRAS/BRAF WT)
- **Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan** (HER2 overexpression, IHC 3+)
- **(Adagrasib or sotorasib) + (cetuximab or panitumumab)** (KRAS G12C)

### Reassess Every 2 Months
→ If converted to resectable: Proceed to resection ± local therapy
→ If remains unresectable: Continue systemic therapy ± consider local therapy for select patients

# Surveillance

## REC-10: Following Operative Management

### Stage I with Full Surgical Staging
- Colonoscopy at 1 year after surgery
  - If advanced adenoma: repeat in 1 year
  - If no advanced adenoma: repeat in 3 years, then every 5 years

### Stage II–IV
| Modality | Frequency |
|----------|-----------|
| History and physical | Every 3–6 mo for 2 y, then every 6 mo for total 5 y |
| CEA | Every 3–6 mo for 2 y, then every 6 mo for total 5 y |
| C/A/P CT | Stage II-III: every 6–12 mo for 5 y; Stage IV: every 3–6 mo × 2 y, then every 6–12 mo |
| Colonoscopy | At 1 y (or 3–6 mo if incomplete preoperative) |
| FDG-PET/CT | NOT recommended |

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>ctDNA is not recommended for surveillance</strong> outside of clinical trials
</div>

# REC-10A: Following Nonoperative Management

## Intensive Surveillance Protocol

| Modality | Frequency |
|----------|-----------|
| History and physical | Every 3–6 mo for 2 y, then every 6 mo for 5 y |
| CEA | Every 3–6 mo for 2 y, then every 6 mo for 5 y |
| DRE and proctoscopy/flexible sigmoidoscopy | Every 3–4 mo for 2 y, then every 6 mo for 5 y |
| MRI rectum | Every 6 mo for up to 3 y |
| CT chest/abdomen | Every 6–12 mo for 5 y |
| CT pelvis | Once no longer doing MRI |
| Colonoscopy | At 1 year following completion of therapy |

<div class="important-box">
<strong>Requires experienced multidisciplinary team and patient commitment to intensive follow-up</strong>
</div>

# REC-11: Recurrence & Workup

## Serial CEA Elevation

### Workup
- Physical exam
- Colonoscopy
- C/A/P CT with contrast
- Consider FDG-PET/CT

### Findings Management

| Finding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| Negative findings | Consider FDG-PET/CT; Re-evaluate CT in 3 months |
| Positive findings | See treatment for isolated pelvic/anastomotic recurrence OR Documented metachronous metastases |

## Documented Metachronous Metastases
- Determine resectability
- Consider FDG-PET/CT
- Test biomarker status (pMMR/MSS vs dMMR/MSI-H)

# REC-11A: Isolated Pelvic/Anastomotic Recurrence

## Treatment by Resectability & Biomarker Status

| Status | Resectable | Unresectable |
|--------|-----------|-------------|
| **dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1** | Resection OR Systemic therapy (REC-18) OR Long-course chemo/RT → Resection | Systemic therapy (REC-18) |
| **pMMR/MSS** | Chemotherapy (FOLFOX/CAPEOX/FOLFIRINOX) → Long-course chemo/RT or Short-course RT → Resection ± IORT | Long-course chemo/RT or Short-course RT → Systemic therapy |

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>Previous RT given:</strong> See Principles of Radiation Therapy (REC-E) for re-irradiation guidance
</div>

# REC-12: Resectable Metachronous Metastases (pMMR/MSS)

## No Previous Chemotherapy

| Approach | Adjuvant Treatment |
|----------|-------------------|
| Resection and/or local therapy | FOLFOX or CAPEOX (preferred) OR Capecitabine or fluorouracil/leucovorin |
| Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (2-3 mo) → Resection/local therapy | FOLFOX or CAPEOX OR Capecitabine OR Fluorouracil/leucovorin OR Observation |

## Previous Chemotherapy
- Resection and/or local therapy → Observation (preferred if previous oxaliplatin-based) OR Systemic therapy ± biologic therapy (REC-F)
- Neoadjuvant chemotherapy → Resection → FOLFOX/CAPEOX OR Capecitabine OR Fluorouracil/leucovorin OR Observation

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Local therapy:</strong> Resection preferred for liver; thermal ablation equivalent for ≤3cm; surgery/thermal ablation/SBRT for lung
</div>

# REC-13: Unresectable Metachronous Metastases (pMMR/MSS)

## Initial Treatment Based on Prior Therapy

### Previous FOLFOX/CAPEOX within past 12 months
- (FOLFIRI or irinotecan) ± bevacizumab [preferred] OR ziv-aflibercept OR ramucirumab
- (FOLFIRI or irinotecan) ± cetuximab or panitumumab (KRAS/NRAS/BRAF WT)
- Encorafenib + (cetuximab or panitumumab) ± FOLFIRI or FOLFOX or CAPEOX (BRAF V600E)
- (Pertuzumab or tucatinib) + trastuzumab (HER2+ and KRAS/NRAS/BRAF WT)
- Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan (HER2 overexpression, IHC 3+)
- (Adagrasib or sotorasib) + (cetuximab or panitumumab) (KRAS G12C)

### Previous FOLFOX/CAPEOX >12 mo OR Previous fluorouracil/leucovorin/capecitabine OR No previous chemotherapy
→ Systemic therapy (REC-F)

## Re-evaluation
→ Every 2 months for conversion to resectable

# dMMR/MSI-H or POLE/POLD1: Overview

## Ultra-Hypermutated Phenotype (TMB >50 mut/Mb)

::: {.incremental}
1. **Localized Disease** (REC-14)
   - Checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy (preferred)
   - Total neoadjuvant therapy alternative

2. **Synchronous Metastatic** (REC-15)
   - Resectable liver/lung: Checkpoint inhibitor (preferred)
   - Other sites: Systemic immunotherapy

3. **Recurrence/Metachronous** (REC-16 through REC-18)
   - Resectable: Checkpoint inhibitor (preferred)
   - Unresectable: Checkpoint inhibitor or combination
:::

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Key distinction:</strong> Immunotherapy is the preferred approach for dMMR/MSI-H disease at all stages
</div>

# REC-14: dMMR/MSI-H — Locally Advanced

## Neoadjuvant/Definitive Immunotherapy (Preferred)

### Checkpoint Inhibitor Immunotherapy (up to 6 months)
→ Re-evaluate disease status every 2-3 months

| Response | Management |
|----------|-----------|
| **Complete clinical response** | Surveillance (REC-10A) |
| **Persistent disease at 6 months** | Long-course chemo/RT OR Short-course RT → Resection or Surveillance (if cCR) |
| **Consistent response** | Continue checkpoint inhibitor |

## Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (Alternative)
- Long-course chemo/RT OR Short-course RT
- → Chemotherapy (FOLFOX/CAPEOX, Consider FOLFIRINOX)
- → Restaging → Resection or Surveillance (if cCR)

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>FOLFIRINOX is not recommended in this setting</strong> for dMMR/MSI-H
</div>

# REC-15: dMMR/MSI-H — Synchronous Metastatic

## Stratification & Treatment

| Finding | Primary Treatment |
|---------|-------------------|
| **Resectable liver only and/or lung only** | REC-16 |
| **Synchronous abdominal/peritoneal metastases** | REC-18 |
| **Synchronous unresectable other sites** | REC-18 |

### Nonobstructing Primary
→ REC-18 (Systemic therapy)

### Obstructed or Imminent Obstruction
→ Resection OR Diverting ostomy OR Bowel bypass OR Stenting → REC-18

<div class="important-box">
Patients not candidates for immunotherapy should be treated as pMMR/MSS
</div>

# REC-16: Resectable Synchronous Liver/Lung (dMMR/MSI-H)

## Neoadjuvant Treatment

### Preferred: Checkpoint Inhibitor Immunotherapy
→ Restaging → 

| Response | Next Step |
|----------|-----------|
| Complete response to immunotherapy | Surveillance (REC-10A) |
| No complete response | Short-course RT (preferred) OR Long-course chemo/RT → Staged/synchronous resection and/or local therapy |

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>Data are limited</strong> for checkpoint inhibitor in neoadjuvant setting; risk of early progression may be higher than chemotherapy (Andre T, NEJM 2020)
</div>

### Alternative (if contraindication to immunotherapy)
- Neoadjuvant chemotherapy: FOLFOX, CAPEOX, or FOLFIRINOX

# REC-17: Resectable Metachronous (dMMR/MSI-H)

## No Previous Immunotherapy

| Approach | Adjuvant Treatment |
|----------|-------------------|
| Checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy (preferred) | Observation OR Resection and/or local therapy |
| Resection and/or local therapy | FOLFOX or CAPEOX |

## Previous Immunotherapy or Contraindication
- Resection and/or local therapy → Observation (preferred if previous oxaliplatin) OR Systemic therapy ± biologic therapy (REC-F)
- Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (FOLFOX/CAPEOX) → Resection → FOLFOX/CAPEOX OR Observation

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Note:</strong> Capecitabine or Fluorouracil/Leucovorin removed as treatment options in Version 1.2026
</div>

# REC-18: Unresectable Metastases (dMMR/MSI-H)

## Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy

### No Prior Immunotherapy
- Checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy (REC-F 5 of 17)
- Re-evaluate disease status every 2–3 months

### Subsequent Treatment (if response)
- Surveillance (REC-10A)
- Surgery ± RT
- Continue immunotherapy
- **Ipilimumab + nivolumab** (if checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy previously received)
- Systemic therapy (REC-F)

### Prior Immunotherapy Received
- Systemic therapy (REC-F)
- **Ipilimumab + nivolumab** (if checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy was previously received)

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>Consider discontinuing checkpoint inhibitor after 2 years</strong> of disease response
</div>

# Principles of Imaging (REC-A)

## Initial Workup/Staging

| Modality | Indication |
|----------|-----------|
| **Pelvis MRI** | T and N staging; with or without contrast; endorectal ultrasound only for T1 or if MRI contraindicated |
| **Chest CT + Abdominal CT or MRI** | Distant metastatic disease assessment |
| **FDG-PET/CT** | NOT routinely indicated; consider if potentially surgically curable M1 or for liver-directed therapy planning |

## Restaging
- Chest CT + Abdominal CT or MRI + Pelvis MRI
- Prior to surgery, adjuvant treatment, or re-evaluation for conversion

## Follow-up/Surveillance
- **Stage I:** Imaging not routinely indicated
- **Stage II-III:** C/A/P CT every 6-12 months for 5 years
- **Stage IV:** C/A/P CT every 3-6 months × 2 years, then every 6-12 months

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Therapy-dependent intervals:</strong> Chemo/RT: assess at 12 weeks, reassess at 16-20 weeks; TNT: assess at 24 weeks, reassess at 34-38 weeks
</div>

# Principles of Pathologic & Molecular Review (REC-B)

## Key Pathologic Parameters

::: {.incremental}
- **Grade** of cancer
- **Depth of invasion** (pT) — based on viable tumor; acellular mucin pools not residual tumor after neoadjuvant therapy
- **Lymph nodes** — number evaluated and positive (minimum 12 for accurate staging)
- **Margins** — proximal, distal, circumferential (CRM), mesenteric
- **CRM** — positive if tumor ≤1mm from margin
- **Neoadjuvant treatment effect** — grade 0 (complete response) to 3 (poor response)
- **Lymphovascular invasion**
- **Perineural invasion (PNI)** — independent prognostic factor
- **Tumor deposits** — record number
- **Tumor budding** — low (0-4), intermediate (5-9), high (≥10) tier
:::

# Molecular Testing Requirements

## Universal Testing (All Patients)

| Test | Indication |
|------|-----------|
| **MMR/MSI** | All newly diagnosed rectal cancer |
| **RAS (KRAS/NRAS)** | All metastatic CRC |
| **BRAF V600E** | All metastatic CRC |
| **HER2 (ERBB2)** | All metastatic CRC |

## Extended Panel Testing (MGPT)
- **POLE/POLD1** — ultra-hypermutated phenotype (TMB >50 mut/Mb)
- **NTRK 1/2/3** — gene fusions (rare, ~0.35%)
- **RET** — gene fusions

## Important Notes
- Testing on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue or blood-based ctDNA
- Do NOT repeat molecular testing after standard cytotoxic chemotherapy
- Consider repeat testing after targeted therapies

<div class="important-box">
<strong>BRAF V600E + MLH1 loss:</strong> Generally excludes Lynch syndrome (but ~1% may still be LS)
</div>

# Principles of Surgery (REC-C)

## Transanal Local Excision Criteria
- <30% circumference; <3cm; clear margin (>3mm)
- Mobile, nonfixed; within 8cm of anal verge
- T1 only; well to moderately differentiated
- No lymphovascular invasion or PNI
- No lymphadenopathy on pretreatment imaging

## Transabdominal Resection (TME)
- Standard component of radical rectal cancer surgery
- Extend 4-5cm below distal edge of tumors
- Distal rectal cancers: negative distal margin 1-2cm acceptable
- Minimally invasive approaches (laparoscopic, robotic) — safe, equivalent outcomes

## ESD (Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection)
- For lesions at risk for submucosally invasive cancer
- Criteria: Type V Kudo pit pattern, depressed component, complex morphology, LST ≥20mm (nongranular) or ≥30mm (granular)
- Curative when: negative margins, submucosal invasion <1000μm, no lymphovascular invasion, low tumor budding, well-moderately differentiated

# Locoregional Therapies (REC-C)

## Liver Metastases
| Modality | Indication |
|----------|-----------|
| **Resection** | Treatment of choice; prioritized over ablation |
| **Thermal ablation** | Equivalent to resection for ≤3cm lesions; reduced toxicity |
| **SBRT** | When other local therapies not possible or patient prefers noninvasive |
| **Y-90 radioembolization** | Chemotherapy-resistant/refractory, predominant hepatic disease |
| **Hepatic arterial infusion** | At experienced institutions; VEGF inhibitor contraindicated |

## Lung Metastases
- Surgery, thermal ablation, and SBRT can be considered
- Based on multidisciplinary discussion and patient preference

## Conversion to Resectable
- Re-evaluate after 2 months of chemotherapy and every 2 months thereafter
- High response rate regimens preferred for potentially convertible disease

# Principles of Perioperative Therapy (REC-D)

## Chemotherapy Regimens

| Regimen | Dosing | Duration |
|---------|--------|----------|
| **Modified FOLFOX6** | Oxaliplatin 85mg/m², LV 400mg/m², 5-FU bolus + 2400mg/m² infusion | Every 2 weeks, up to 6 months |
| **CAPEOX** | Oxaliplatin 130mg/m², Capecitabine 1000mg/m² BID × 14 days | Every 3 weeks, up to 6 months |
| **FOLFIRINOX** | Oxaliplatin 85mg/m², LV 400mg/m², Irinotecan 180mg/m², 5-FU 2400mg/m² | Every 2 weeks |
| **Modified FOLFIRINOX** | Irinotecan reduced to 150mg/m² | Every 2 weeks |

## Concurrent with RT
- **5-FU:** 225mg/m² IV continuous, Days 1-5 or 1-7 for 5 weeks
- **Capecitabine:** 825mg/m² PO BID, Monday-Friday, on radiation days only

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>FOLFIRINOX recommended over FOLFOXIRI</strong> for U.S. patients due to lower 5-FU dose (2400mg/m² vs 3200mg/m²)
</div>

# Principles of Radiation Therapy (REC-E)

## General Principles
- Fluoropyrimidine (oral or continuous infusion) concurrent with conventionally fractionated RT
- **Endorectal brachytherapy** can be considered for dose escalation in select patients
- **IMRT preferred** for reirradiation, postoperative cases, or unique anatomical situations
- **IORT** may be considered for very close or positive margins after resection

## RT Dosing
| Regimen | Dose |
|---------|------|
| **Long-course** | 45–54 Gy in 25–30 fractions to pelvis; SIB: 45Gy pelvis + 50-54Gy tumor bed |
| **Short-course** | 25 Gy in 5 fractions |
| **Boost** | 5.4-9.0 Gy in 3-5 fractions (after 45Gy for resectable cancers) |

## Small Bowel Constraints
- Long-course: Dmax ≤55Gy, V45Gy ≤150cc, V50Gy ≤30cc
- Short-course: D0.03cc ≤26.5Gy (up to 28.75Gy acceptable), V20Gy ≤50cc

<div class="important-box">
<strong>For locally recurrent disease after prior pelvis RT:</strong> Consider hyperfractionated pelvic re-irradiation or proton beam therapy
</div>

# Systemic Therapy: pMMR/MSS (REC-F)

## KRAS WT / NRAS WT / BRAF WT

### Initial Therapy
- CAPEOX ± bevacizumab
- CAPEOX + (cetuximab or panitumumab)
- FOLFIRI ± bevacizumab
- FOLFIRI + (cetuximab or panitumumab)
- FOLFIRINOX ± bevacizumab
- FOLFOX ± bevacizumab
- FOLFOX + (cetuximab or panitumumab)

### Subsequent Therapy
| Prior Treatment | Options |
|-----------------|---------|
| **Prior Oxaliplatin** | FOLFIRI ± (cetuximab/panitumumab/bevacizumab/ziv-aflibercept/ramucirumab) |
| **Prior Irinotecan** | FOLFOX/CAPEOX ± bevacizumab; Irinotecan + (cetuximab or panitumumab) |
| **Beyond Second Line** | Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan (HER2+); (Pertuzumab/tucatinib)+trastuzumab; Tumor-agnostic; TAS-102 ± bevacizumab; Fruquintinib; Regorafenib |

# Systemic Therapy: Mutated RAS or BRAF V600E

## (KRAS or NRAS mutation) + BRAF WT

### Initial Therapy
- CAPEOX ± bevacizumab
- FOLFIRI ± bevacizumab
- FOLFIRINOX ± bevacizumab
- FOLFOX ± bevacizumab

### Less Intensive
- Capecitabine ± bevacizumab
- Fluorouracil/leucovorin ± bevacizumab
- **Adagrasib or Sotorasib monotherapy** (KRAS G12C)

### Beyond Second Line
- (Adagrasib or sotorasib) + (cetuximab or panitumumab) (KRAS G12C)

## KRAS WT / NRAS WT / BRAF V600E mutation

### Preferred Initial
- **FOLFIRI/Encorafenib + (cetuximab or panitumumab)**
- **FOLFOX/Encorafenib + (cetuximab or panitumumab)**

### Other Recommended
- CAPEOX ± bevacizumab
- **CAPEOX/Encorafenib + (cetuximab or panitumumab)**
- FOLFIRI ± bevacizumab
- FOLFIRINOX ± bevacizumab
- FOLFOX ± bevacizumab

<div class="highlight-box">
<strong>Encorafenib + (cetuximab or panitumumab)</strong> as less intensive option; may add FOLFOX/CAPEOX/FOLFIRI
</div>

# Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy (dMMR/MSI-H)

## PD-1 Inhibitors
- Cemiplimab-rwlc
- Dostarlimab-gxly
- Nivolumab
- Pembrolizumab
- **Penpulimab-kcqx** *(new in v1.2026)*
- Retifanlimab-dlwr
- Tislelizumab-jsgr
- Toripalimab-tpzi

## PD-L1 Inhibitors *(new/expanded in v1.2026)*
- **Atezolizumab**
- **Avelumab**
- **Cosibelimab-ipdl**
- **Durvalumab**

## Combination
- **Ipilimumab + Nivolumab** (PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade)

<div class="warning-box">
<strong>Follow closely for 10 weeks to assess response.</strong> Some agents included based on presumed class effect from other cancer types.
</div>

# Tumor-Agnostic Therapies

| Biomarker | Therapy |
|-----------|---------|
| **HER2 overexpression (IHC 3+)** | Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan |
| **NTRK 1/2/3 gene fusion** | Entrectinib; Larotrectinib; Repotrectinib |
| **RET gene fusion** | Selpercatinib |

## KRAS G12C Mutations
| Setting | Regimen |
|---------|---------|
| Monotherapy | Adagrasib 600mg BID; Sotorasib 960mg daily |
| + EGFR inhibitor | Adagrasib + (cetuximab or panitumumab); Sotorasib + (cetuximab or panitumumab) |

## HER2-Targeted (KRAS/NRAS/BRAF WT)
- Pertuzumab + Trastuzumab
- Tucatinib + Trastuzumab

# Principles of Survivorship (REC-G)

## Long-Term Follow-Up Care

### Care Planning
- Develop survivorship care plan with treatment summary
- Define roles: oncologist vs. primary care provider
- Include: treatment summary, expected toxicities, surveillance recommendations, health behavior recommendations

### Management of Late Sequelae
| Issue | Management |
|-------|-----------|
| **Bowel dysfunction** | Anti-diarrheals, bulk-forming agents, diet manipulation, pelvic floor rehab |
| **Oxaliplatin neuropathy** | Duloxetine for painful neuropathy (not numbness/tingling); pain specialist for refractory |
| **Urogenital dysfunction** | Screen for sexual/urinary issues; refer to urologist/gynecologist |
| **Bone density** | Consider DEXA after pelvic radiation |

## Healthy Lifestyle
- Maintain healthy body weight
- **≥150 minutes moderate-vigorous physical activity per week**
- Plant-based diet emphasis
- Daily aspirin 325mg for secondary prevention
- Smoking cessation

# Principles of Nonoperative Management (REC-H)

## Watch and Wait Criteria

<div class="important-box">
<strong>NOM is recommended ONLY at centers with experienced multidisciplinary teams and for patients committed to intensive surveillance</strong>
</div>

### Requirements
- Accurate assessment of clinical, radiologic, and pathologic findings
- Determine patient eligibility for NOM
- Close monitoring of treatment responses
- Prompt identification of surgical needs
- Comprehensive understanding of watchful waiting literature

### Complete Clinical Response (cCR)
- No evidence of residual disease on DRE, rectal MRI, and direct endoscopic evaluation
- Correlates with durable response
- Local excision NOT routinely recommended for clear cCR (may introduce unnecessary risk)

### Surveillance
- See REC-10A for intensive surveillance protocol

## Key Takeaways

1. **Personalized approach based on biomarker status** — pMMR/MSS vs dMMR/MSI-H/POLE/POLD1
2. **Total neoadjuvant therapy** — standard for locally advanced pMMR/MSS
3. **Immunotherapy priority** — for dMMR/MSI-H at all stages
4. **Organ preservation** — watch and wait for complete clinical response in select patients
5. **Expanded biomarker testing** — MGPT for rare actionable mutations
6. **Aspirin for PI3K-altered stage II-III** — new recommendation in v2.2026
7. **Thermal ablation equivalence** — for small liver metastases (≤3cm)
8. **Intensive surveillance** — required for nonoperative management
